summary: Construct the Smith restriction functor from equivariant étale sheaves to a cyclic Tate quotient, its relative localization and six-operation comparisons, and the normalized integral Tate-parity lifting used in cyclic Satake base change. The final comparison identifies this functor with diagonal restriction of tilting representations under modular equal-characteristic geometric Satake. The plan separates valid ordinary coefficient reduction from false equivariant fullness, character equality from natural dual-group equivariance, and objectwise integral comparisons from their unresolved naturality. It also owns the general algebra Tate diagonal and Frobenius linearization needed by the global and local consumers.

nodes.title: Coefficient and cyclic-action conventions
nodes.statement: A coefficient datum consists of an odd prime p, a separably closed geometric field F with p invertible, k=an algebraic closure of F_p, O=W(k), and C_p with specified generator σ. Use Λ=k, O/p^m or O, as individually stated. Write A_Λ=Λ[C_p] and N=Σ_{i=0}^{p−1}σ^i. Ordinary coefficient actions are Λ-linear; arithmetic semilinear actions are separately marked. Goodness means p does not divide any coefficient of a highest root in each irreducible dual root system. Type A has no excluded primes, B/C/D exclude 2, G₂/F₄/E₆/E₇ exclude 2,3, and E₈ excludes 2,3,5.
hypotheses: Conventions C0–C4 in the reader apply, restricted to the coefficients, support and equivariance stated here.

nodes.title: Admissible geometric actions
nodes.statement: For a separated locally finite type F-scheme Y, an admissible C_p-action is an action for which every orbit is contained in an invariant affine open; equivalently use an invariant affine open cover in the cases considered. Define Y^σ as the scheme-theoretic equalizer of σ and identity, and Y/C_p as the glued affine invariant quotient. The complement of Y^σ is a free C_p-space because p is prime; in characteristic different from p its quotient is a finite étale C_p-torsor. For ind-schemes require an invariant closed filtration by finite-type pieces.

nodes.title: Separate Tor bounds for compact support and open direct image
nodes.statement: Let A=k[C_p] or (O/p^m)[C_p], and let f:Y→S be separated of finite type, with geometric fibres of dimension ≤d, under the torsion étale projection formula and the bound cd_c(f)≤2d. If K has A-Tor amplitude [a,b], then Rf!K has amplitude [a,b+2d]. For a quasi-compact open immersion j:U→X into a finite-dimensional noetherian scheme, Rj* preserves finite A-Tor dimension when the relevant ambient local étale cohomological dimension is uniformly bounded. Its bound is that ambient bound, not 2 times the relative dimension of j. At adic O-level require one compatible finite-level system, a uniform bound and the derived-limit/projection-formula comparisons.
hypotheses: Conventions C0–C4 in the reader apply, restricted to the coefficients, support and equivariance stated here.

nodes.title: A free geometric quotient produces flat complexes
nodes.statement: If C_p acts freely and admissibly on Y, q:Y→Y/C_p is its finite étale quotient and E∈D^b_σ(Y;Λ) has finite Λ-Tor dimension, then q_*E, with its quotient C_p-action, has locally a bounded induced A_Λ-resolution and is flat over A_Λ. For Λ=k the coefficient Tor hypothesis is automatic. The hypothesis is geometric equivariance, not a second independent C_p-action on an arbitrary sheaf.
hypotheses: Conventions C0–C4 in the reader apply, restricted to the coefficients, support and equivariance stated here.

proofSteps: Étale locally trivialize the torsor; descent identifies E with identical coefficient complexes on p sheets. Pushforward is induction from Λ to A_Λ. Tensor a Λ-flat resolution with the regular representation.
acceptance: For p disjoint points permuted cyclically and an equivariant constant Λ-sheaf, q_* gives the regular Λ[C_p]-module. Giving p constant summands an unrelated trivial coefficient action fails this test.

nodes.title: Modular equal-characteristic geometric Satake
nodes.statement: For a connected reductive H over separably closed F of characteristic different from p, the spherical perverse category P_{L^+H}(Gr_H;k) with fusion commutativity is tensor-equivalent to finite-dimensional rational Rep_k(Ĥ), where Ĥ is the pinned integral dual group base changed to k. The O-flat perverse subcategory has the corresponding tensor equivalence with finite free O-representations of Ĥ_O. The geometry is the scheme-theoretic equal-characteristic affine Grassmannian, not the B_dR^+ Grassmannian. The fibre functor is total cohomology with the usual parity sign correction to symmetry.
hypotheses: Conventions C0–C4 in the reader apply, restricted to the coefficients, support and equivariance stated here.

sources.match: For a connected reductive H over separably closed F of characteristic different from p, the spherical perverse category P_{L^+H}(Gr_H;k) with fusion commutativity is tensor-equivalent to finite-dimensional rational Rep_k(Ĥ), where Ĥ is the pinned integral dual group base changed to k. The proof outline records corrections and any additional obligation.

proofSteps: Reuse the existing BD Grassmannian, bounded Schubert geometry and fusion correspondences. Prove weight-functor exactness and tensor compatibility with torsion/integral coefficients by the semi-infinite dimension estimates and Künneth formula. Reconstruct the integral Hopf algebra using projective generators on finite Schubert unions, prove base change, and identify its root datum with the already owned dual group. MV07 Theorem 14.1 gives the étale variant; explicitly supply the O-adic extension using compatible finite levels, and separably closed to algebraically closed invariance. G2 records these coefficient/transport obligations.
acceptance: For a split torus, point sheaves indexed by coweights correspond to one-dimensional characters; fusion adds coweights. For H=PGL₂ the IC/parity representation of the dual SL₂ has the expected highest weight, so using the original root datum instead of the dual is detected.

nodes.title: Satake standards and coefficient change
nodes.statement: Fix a Borel and dominant λ. Under modular-satake, the perverse standard ^pj_!Λ[dim Gr^λ] corresponds to the Weyl module Δ(λ), and the perverse costandard ^pj_*Λ[dim Gr^λ] to ∇(λ), with the canonical highest-weight map matched. On O-flat objects the k-reduction comparison is derived tensor k⊗^L_O, with ordinary representation reduction on the other side. Do not assert that derived reduction of an arbitrary integral perverse object stays in the perverse heart.
hypotheses: Conventions C0–C4 in the reader apply, restricted to the coefficients, support and equivariance stated here.

sources.locator: MV07 Proposition 13.1 and Corollary 13.2, pp.39–40; Feng24 §4.5, p.23
sources.match: Fix a Borel and dominant λ. The proof outline records corrections and any additional obligation.

proofSteps: Use the universal properties on each saturated highest-weight ideal, evaluated by the λ-weight functor. Compare standard/costandard maps and integral projective generators before extending scalars. Track derived tensor for torsion objects.
acceptance: At λ=0 both standard and costandard are the unit. For dual SL₂ in characteristic 3, distinguish Δ(3) from ∇(3); do not identify them by semisimplicity or an integral arbitrary-object reduction argument.

nodes.title: The category of rational tilting representations
nodes.statement: Using the Weyl and dual-Weyl modules and highest-weight filtrations supplied by LP3, Tilt_Λ(Ĥ) is the full additive subcategory of finite free rational Ĥ_Λ-modules admitting both a finite Δ-filtration and a finite ∇-filtration. For Λ=k, finite free means finite-dimensional. Its exact structure is inherited from rational representations; it is closed under direct summands, not under all kernels and cokernels. Use the integral reductive group representation carrier, not arbitrary representations of the discrete group of k-points.
hypotheses: Conventions C0–C4 in the reader apply, restricted to the coefficients, support and equivariance stated here.

sources.match: Using the Weyl and dual-Weyl modules and highest-weight filtrations supplied by LP3, Tilt_Λ(Ĥ) is the full additive subcategory of finite free rational Ĥ_Λ-modules admitting both a finite Δ-filtration and a finite ∇-filtration. The proof outline records corrections and any additional obligation.

proofSteps: Import the highest-weight predicates, and define their intersection as a full subcategory. API must preserve the algebraic comodule structure on every morphism.
acceptance: The trivial representation is tilting, with both filtrations of length one.
For a split torus every finite-dimensional rational representation is tilting, with its finite character decomposition.

For SL₂ in characteristic 3, the Weyl module Δ(3) has an exact sequence 0→L(1)→Δ(3)→L(3)→0 of two-dimensional simple factors; ∇(3) has the reversed Loewy layers. Thus Δ(3) is not tilting, while T(3) has character ch Δ(3)+ch Δ(1) and dimension 6.

nodes.statement: Tensor products of finite-dimensional rational tilting modules for a split connected reductive group over k are tilting. For a product group, external tensor products of indecomposable tiltings give its indecomposable tiltings. The characters ch T(λ) are triangular with leading dominant weight λ of multiplicity one, so equal characters imply isomorphism for finite direct sums of tiltings. Restriction to a maximal torus is faithful, but it is generally not full.

nodes.title: Even stratifications and pariversities
nodes.statement: A JMW stratification S of Y has finitely many connected smooth locally closed strata, the usual frontier condition, and the following coefficient condition for Λ=k or O: for finite free local systems L,L′ on each stratum, every Ext^n(L,L′) is finite free over Λ and vanishes for odd n. A pariversity † assigns an element of Z/2 to each stratum; the dimension pariversity is dim(Y_λ) mod 2. Simple connectivity is an additional hypothesis used for lifting, not part of the general definition.

nodes.title: Parity complexes and parity sheaves
nodes.statement: An object E∈D^b_S(Y;Λ) is *-even for † if each i_λ*E has finite free local-system cohomology only in degrees congruent to †(λ); !-even uses i_λ!E. Even means both, odd means E[1] is even, and parity means a direct sum of an even and an odd object. A parity sheaf E(λ,L) is an indecomposable parity object supported on closure(Y_λ) whose restriction to Y_λ is L[dim Y_λ], for an indecomposable finite free local system L. Existence is an independent theorem.

nodes.title: Uniqueness and Krull–Schmidt for parity extensions
nodes.statement: In the finite JMW setting with complete local coefficient ring Λ, parity objects have Krull–Schmidt decompositions. Every indecomposable parity object has one irreducible support closure(Y_λ), restricts there to one indecomposable local system shifted by an integer, and is determined up to isomorphism by that restriction and support. This proves uniqueness of E(λ,L), not its existence.
hypotheses: Conventions C0–C4 in the reader apply, restricted to the coefficients, support and equivariance stated here.

sources.locator: JMW14 Theorem 2.12, pp.7–8; Feng24 Theorem 4.1, p.20
sources.match: In the finite JMW setting with complete local coefficient ring Λ, parity objects have Krull–Schmidt decompositions. The proof outline records corrections and any additional obligation.

proofSteps: Induct over strata using odd-Hom vanishing to extend maps between restrictions. Endomorphism rings of finite-support parity objects are finite over the complete local coefficient ring, so idempotents split and the usual local-ring criterion gives Krull–Schmidt. The dense-stratum inverse lifts modulo the boundary radical.
acceptance: On a point over complete local O, the only normalized rank-one extension is O. Uniqueness must not imply existence for an arbitrary stratified singular variety; the Grassmannian existence theorem is an additional input.

nodes.title: Parity extensions on the equal-characteristic Grassmannian
nodes.statement: The L^+H-orbit stratification of every finite Schubert union in Gr_H is JMW for Λ=k,O and has simply connected strata. Its normalized parity extensions exist for all dominant coweights and trivial finite free local systems. They admit compatible L^+H-equivariant structures in the precise non-torsion-prime setting of JMW16 Theorem 1.4. Under the odd good-prime hypothesis of Feng24, prove that the orbit-constructible normalized category used below has the required equivariant realization; do not identify the full equivariant derived category with the orbit-constructible one.
hypotheses: Conventions C0–C4 in the reader apply, restricted to the coefficients, support and equivariance stated here.

sources.locator: Feng24 §4.1, p.20 and §4.5, pp.22–23; JMW16 Theorem 1.4, pp.2–3
sources.match: The L^+H-orbit stratification of every finite Schubert union in Gr_H is JMW for Λ=k,O and has simply connected strata. The proof outline records corrections and any additional obligation.

proofSteps: Build Bott–Samelson parity pushforwards on affine flag varieties, then take the appropriate summands on the partial flag/Grassmannian. Check evenness, the local-system condition and integral lifting on each bounded piece. Compare étale and complex proofs, including non-torsion/good-prime equivariance and passage to separably closed F. These proof inputs are the explicit transport contract G2.
acceptance: For a torus every stratum is a point and its extension is Λ. For a GL₂ minuscule closed Schubert P¹ the normalized extension is Λ[1]. Check ordinary Hom separately from equivariant Hom.

nodes.title: Normalized parity sheaves are tilting Satake objects
nodes.statement: For odd p good for the root system of Ĥ (equivalently H), every normalized k- or O-parity sheaf on Gr_H is perverse. Modular Satake induces Parity^0_{(L^+H)}(Gr_H;k)≅Tilt_k(Ĥ), with the chosen equivariant realization when required. The integral version uses O-flat perverse sheaves. The characteristic assumption is goodness, not the larger bounds in JMW16 Theorem 1.8.
hypotheses: Conventions C0–C4 in the reader apply, restricted to the coefficients, support and equivariance stated here.

sources.locator: Feng24 Theorem 4.8, p.23; MR18 Corollary 1.6, pp.6–7 and proof §6.5, p.60
sources.match: For odd p good for the root system of Ĥ (equivalently H), every normalized k- or O-parity sheaf on Gr_H is perverse. The proof outline records corrections and any additional obligation.

proofSteps: Use MR18 Theorem 1.1: the mixed/parity affine-Grassmannian category is related to the exotic coherent category on the Springer resolution of the dual group, compatibly with grading and tilting generators. Its Corollary 1.6 establishes perversity for every good prime, reducing along central isogenies and products. The exotic/Soergel proof engine and its étale transport are not supplied by the characteristic-zero Springer roadmap; G3 records this exact missing foundation. Once perversity holds, Δ/∇-filtrations characterize the Satake images as tilting.
acceptance: For the GL₂ minuscule P¹ stratum, k[1] is perverse and maps to the corresponding fundamental tilting representation. Check the hypothesis is odd good p, rather than the larger source-specific sufficient bounds.

nodes.title: External products of normalized Grassmannian parity sheaves
nodes.statement: For G=H^r, every normalized O-parity object on Gr_G≅(Gr_H)^r is a finite direct sum of E(λ₁)⊠⋯⊠E(λ_r). The external product is the normalized indecomposable extension on the product stratum. Its stalk and costalk cohomology are the graded tensor products of the corresponding finite free O-modules, including the Koszul symmetry signs.
hypotheses: Conventions C0–C4 in the reader apply, restricted to the coefficients, support and equivariance stated here.

sources.locator: Feng24 Lemma 4.14, pp.24–25, corrected for normalized parity objects; Theorem 4.8, p.23
sources.match: For G=H^r, every normalized O-parity object on Gr_G≅(Gr_H)^r is a finite direct sum of E(λ₁)⊠⋯⊠E(λ_r). The proof outline records corrections and any additional obligation.

proofSteps: Use the Künneth theorem for finite free stalks and costalks, and dense-stratum normalization. Indecomposability follows either from the product tilting classification under Satake or from the local endomorphism criterion. This direct-sum decomposition replaces the invalid t-exact filtration argument in the printed proof.
acceptance: The product of the GL₂ minuscule generators is O_{(P¹)^r}[r] and has rank-one dense-stratum restriction. A direct sum of two generators stays a direct sum and is not mislabeled indecomposable.

nodes.title: The graded Hom formula and its composition law
nodes.statement: For bounded constructible O-complexes E,F in the LL integral Tate setting, with trivial coefficient C_p-action and the finite-support coefficient hypotheses, Hom_{Perf(Y;TO)}(T*ε*E,T*ε*F)≅⊕_{i∈Z}Hom_{D^b(Y;k)}(k⊗^L E,(k⊗^L F)[2i]). Composition adds the indices using shifts. Require the stratified version with finite Hom groups and nilpotence of the positive-degree endomorphism ideal for normalized parity inputs. The category is Krull–Schmidt under the finite-stratification, complete-local and simply-connected-strata assumptions used by LL.
hypotheses: Conventions C0–C4 in the reader apply, restricted to the coefficients, support and equivariance stated here.

sources.locator: LL21 Proposition 4.6.1, pp.14–15 and Proposition 5.5.2, pp.21–22; Feng24 (4.2), p.22

The proof outline records corrections and any additional obligation.

proofSteps: Compare the periodic complete resolution with derived reduction, then compute quotient morphisms by stabilized Hom. Check naturality and the index-addition composition formula before projecting any grading. Carry the proof through the étale coefficient setting via G2. Finite support and bounded Hom ensure the nonnegative endomorphism algebra has nilpotent positive ideal in the perverse case.
acceptance: For E=O_{P¹}[1], the Tate endomorphisms have index-zero k and index-one H²(P¹;k). Composition of homogeneous classes adds indices; at a point only index zero remains for degree-zero inputs.

nodes.title: Tate parity and Tate-parity sheaves
nodes.statement: In Perf_S(Y;TO), an object K is *-Tate-even when T^{†(λ)+1}(i_λ*K)=0 for each λ, and !-Tate-even uses i_λ!K. Tate-even requires both; Tate-odd means a shift by one is even, and Tate-parity means their direct sum. A Tate-parity sheaf is an indecomposable such object whose dense-stratum restriction is T*ε*L[dim Y_λ] for an indecomposable O-free local system L. The integral coefficient ring O is essential: the mod-p Tate unit has nonzero odd cohomology.
hypotheses: Conventions C0–C4 in the reader apply, restricted to the coefficients, support and equivariance stated here.

sources.locator: Definition 4.2 and Definition 4.4, pp.20–21; LL21 Definition 5.3.1, p.20
sources.match: In Perf_S(Y;TO), an object K is *-Tate-even when T^{†(λ)+1}(i_λ*K)=0 for each λ, and !-Tate-even uses i_λ!K. The proof outline records corrections and any additional obligation.

proofSteps: Define vanishing of the opposite parity of Tate cohomology on both restrictions. Normalized dense-stratum data is specified separately from arbitrary shifts and from existence.
acceptance: At a point T*O is Tate-even and T*O[1] is Tate-odd.
A regular O[C_p]-module projects to zero, hence satisfies both even and odd vanishing conditions.
Replacing O by k makes the trivial Tate unit have odd Tate cohomology and fails the intended even-unit test.

nodes.title: Uniqueness of Tate-parity extensions
nodes.statement: In the finite JMW integral Tate setting with simply connected strata and the stated finite-Hom hypotheses, an indecomposable Tate-parity object has support the closure of one stratum and is determined by its restriction to the dense stratum. Existence is separate. If E(λ,L) is an O-parity sheaf with no negative self-Ext, then T*ε*E is the corresponding indecomposable Tate-parity sheaf.
hypotheses: Conventions C0–C4 in the reader apply, restricted to the coefficients, support and equivariance stated here.

sources.locator: Feng24 Proposition 4.3 and Proposition 4.5, pp.21–22; LL21 Theorems 5.5.6 and 5.6.4, pp.22–24
sources.match: In the finite JMW integral Tate setting with simply connected strata and the stated finite-Hom hypotheses, an indecomposable Tate-parity object has support the closure of one stratum and is determined by its restriction to the dense stratum. The proof outline records corrections and any additional obligation.

proofSteps: Repeat support induction with Tate odd-Hom vanishing. For the inflated parity sheaf use the graded Hom formula: its degree-zero endomorphism ring is local, negative degrees vanish and the positive ideal is nilpotent. Thus its full endomorphism ring is local.
acceptance: At a point the integral Tate unit is the normalized even generator. On P¹ the inflated normalized parity extension is indecomposable because its positive endomorphism ideal is nilpotent, even though that ideal is nonzero.

nodes.title: Modular reduction on the non-equivariant parity category
nodes.statement: For a finite JMW stratification with simply connected strata, suppose all normalized O- and k-parity extensions exist. Then F=k⊗^L_O sends O-parity extensions to the corresponding k-parity extensions; for parity E,F′, Hom_O(E,F′) is finite free and k⊗_O Hom_O(E,F′)≅Hom_k(FE,FF′). Consequently Parity^0_S(Y;O)⊗_O k→Parity^0_S(Y;k) is an equivalence of additive categories. This statement is about the non-C_p-equivariant orbit-constructible category. Arbitrary C_p-equivariant reduction is not full.
hypotheses: Conventions C0–C4 in the reader apply, restricted to the coefficients, support and equivariance stated here.

sources.locator: JMW14 Proposition 2.39 and (2.13), pp.17–18; corrected Feng24 Lemma 4.16, p.26
sources.match: For a finite JMW stratification with simply connected strata, suppose all normalized O- and k-parity extensions exist. The proof outline records corrections and any additional obligation.

proofSteps: Use free even local-system Hom and induction across strata for Hom base change. Complete-local idempotent lifting and the existence/uniqueness of all parity extensions give essential surjectivity. For the equivariant non-example, the O[C_p]-augmentation ideal I has I^{C_p}=0, but (I/pI)^{C_p}≠0. This obstruction cannot be removed by forgetting the difference between equivariant and ordinary Hom.
acceptance: At a point ordinary Hom(O,O) reduces to Hom(k,k). The augmentation ideal I has I^{C_p}=0 but (I/pI)^{C_p}≠0; this rejects full equivariant reduction without affecting the ordinary equivalence.

nodes.title: Normalized parity categories
nodes.statement: Parity^0_S(Y;Λ) is the full additive closure of unshifted normalized parity sheaves E(λ,L). Parity^0_S(Y;TO) is defined similarly using Tate-parity sheaves. For the lifting functor require all parity extensions to exist and the cross-negative-Hom condition Hom(E(λ,L),E(μ,L′)[n])=0 for all pairs and every n<0, together with the same condition after reduction. On Gr_H it follows from perversity, once parity-tilting has been proved.
hypotheses: Conventions C0–C4 in the reader apply, restricted to the coefficients, support and equivariance stated here.

proofSteps: Take additive closures without adjoining arbitrary shifts. Distinguish negative self-Ext, enough for individual indecomposability, from cross-negative-Hom, needed for a functor on the whole additive category.

T*O[2]≅T*O is normalized in the Tate category, but O[2] is not normalized in the ordinary category.
Two perverse parity sheaves have no negative cross-Hom, so the full normalized Grassmannian category satisfies the lifting hypothesis.

nodes.title: Lifting normalized Tate parity
nodes.statement: Under the hypotheses of normalized-parity, construct an additive k-linear functor L:Parity^0_S(Y;TO)→Parity^0_S(Y;k), taking E_T(λ,L₀) to E(λ,L₀/pL₀). On Hom use projection to index zero in integral-tate-hom, extended by matrices over finite sums. There is a natural isomorphism L T*ε*≅F on normalized ordinary parity objects and their ordinary morphisms. There is no natural inverse identity T*ε*L≅F on all Tate morphisms.

nodes.title: The cyclic fixed Grassmannian is diagonal
nodes.statement: For G=H^p with σ rotating factors, Gr_G≅(Gr_H)^p and Gr_G^σ≅Gr_H by the diagonal map, as ind-schemes on test rings. The stratum indexed by (λ₁,…,λ_p) meets this fixed locus exactly when all λ_i are equal, in which case the intersection is Gr_H^λ. Its dimension is d_λ on H and p d_λ on G, so the two dimension pariversities agree for odd p.
hypotheses: Conventions C0–C4 in the reader apply, restricted to the coefficients, support and equivariance stated here.

sources.match: For G=H^p with σ rotating factors, Gr_G≅(Gr_H)^p and Gr_G^σ≅Gr_H by the diagonal map, as ind-schemes on test rings. The proof outline records corrections and any additional obligation.

proofSteps: Apply the product description of loop groups and positive loops to the fppf quotient; test-ring fixed points force all components equal. Use the imported dimension formula d_λ=⟨2ρ,λ⟩. Equality mod two is not equality of the integer shifts.
acceptance: For H=G_m the fixed coweight tuples are exactly (ν,…,ν). For a minuscule H-stratum of dimension 1, its p-fold source stratum has dimension p, hence equal parity for odd p but a different integer normalization.

nodes.title: The cyclic convolution norm
nodes.statement: On the spherical symmetric monoidal category for G=H^p, define Nm(E)=E*σE*⋯*σ^{p−1}E with σ-linearization given by cyclic rotation through the fusion symmetry. On maps take the corresponding product of the σ-translates of a map. Define it on all k-Satake objects and on O-flat normalized parity objects. It is a plain functor to the σ-equivariant category; it is neither additive nor O-linear before Smith projection.
hypotheses: Conventions C0–C4 in the reader apply, restricted to the coefficients, support and equivariance stated here.

sources.match: On the spherical symmetric monoidal category for G=H^p, define Nm(E)=E*σE*⋯*σ^{p−1}E with σ-linearization given by cyclic rotation through the fusion symmetry. The proof outline records corrections and any additional obligation.

proofSteps: Use fusion associativity and the sign-corrected symmetry to construct the cyclic linearization and prove its p-th power is the identity. On normalized parity objects tensor closure under Satake gives closure of the convolution norm.

Nm(a·id_E)=a^p·id_{Nm(E)}, so ordinary scalar linearity fails for general a∈k.

nodes.title: Trivial and free cyclic summands in norm stalks
nodes.statement: For E a normalized O-parity object on Gr_{H^p}, the stalk and costalk cohomology of Nm(E) at every diagonal fixed point has a C_p-stable filtration whose associated graded is a direct sum of trivial O-free modules and free O[C_p]-modules. The statement here is restricted to the normalized Grassmannian parity objects used in BC. It does not assert the printed Lemma 4.14 for every integral Satake object.
hypotheses: Conventions C0–C4 in the reader apply, restricted to the coefficients, support and equivariance stated here.

sources.locator: Lemma 4.14, pp.24–25, with the external-product replacement
sources.match: For E a normalized O-parity object on Gr_{H^p}, the stalk and costalk cohomology of Nm(E) at every diagonal fixed point has a C_p-stable filtration whose associated graded is a direct sum of trivial O-free modules and free O[C_p]-modules. The proof outline records corrections and any additional obligation.

proofSteps: Decompose E into finite sums of external products of normalized parity extensions. For one external product, rotation and factorwise convolution give an external p-th power of a single parity object on H, whose finite free stalk and costalk cohomology have a Künneth basis. Cyclic permutation of basis tensors has orbits of size one or p. Koszul signs on a constant p-tuple multiply to +1 for odd p; on a length-p orbit absorb signs into a regular-module basis. Mixed summands from expanding a direct sum form induced cyclic orbits. No perverse filtration is pulled back through i*, and Nm is never applied to an exact sequence as an additive functor.
acceptance: For a stalk with O-basis e₀,e₁ and p=3, the eight tensor words form two fixed words and two free orbits. On an odd-degree basis vector the sign of the length-three cycle is +1. Mixed direct-sum summands are induced.

nodes.title: Smith preserves parity with the cyclic stalk criterion
nodes.statement: Let Y be a finite-dimensional smooth-stratified JMW variety with tame admissible C_p-action preserving each relevant stratum. If E is an equivariant O-parity object and its fixed-point stalk and costalk cohomology have C_p-stable filtrations with trivial O-free or free O[C_p] graded pieces, then Psm(E) is Tate-parity for the induced strata and induced pariversity. Assume the induced fixed stratification is JMW for the classification/lifting applications. Applied to Nm on Gr_{H^p}, this produces normalized Tate parity on Gr_H.
hypotheses: Conventions C0–C4 in the reader apply, restricted to the coefficients, support and equivariance stated here.

sources.match: Let Y be a finite-dimensional smooth-stratified JMW variety with tame admissible C_p-action preserving each relevant stratum. The proof outline records corrections and any additional obligation.

proofSteps: For stalks use the trivial/free Tate formulas and the long exact sequence. For costalks use the !-presentation of Smith and the smooth-pair Gysin comparison. A tame finite-order automorphism has smooth fixed subschemes on a smooth stratum: formal lifting obstructions are averaged because p is invertible in F; its tangent is the fixed tangent subspace. The codimension purity shift is even. On the Grassmannian, p d_λ≡d_λ mod 2, while the difference of the two normalization shifts is even and hence disappears only in the Tate quotient.
acceptance: For the norm of a rank-one point sheaf, the fixed stalk is the trivial O-module and becomes the even Tate unit. A free orbit summand becomes zero. Compare the shifted dimension normalization for odd p explicitly.

nodes.title: Additivity and Frobenius semilinearity on morphisms
nodes.statement: On the ordinary normalized O-parity category of Gr_G, D=Psm∘Nm takes values in normalized Tate parity and is additive on objects and morphisms: D(f+g)=D(f)+D(g) and D(a f)=ā^p D(f), for a∈O and ā its image in k. Its canonical biproduct identifications are natural in both arguments. In particular D kills p times every Hom group. Only ordinary source parity morphisms are asserted here, with their norm-generated equivariant morphisms in the intermediate category.
hypotheses: Conventions C0–C4 in the reader apply, restricted to the coefficients, support and equivariance stated here.

sources.locator: §4.6.3, pp.26–27 and §A.3, p.57; extra morphism obligation identified by REV-PAPER-FENG-24
sources.match: On the ordinary normalized O-parity category of Gr_G, D=Psm∘Nm takes values in normalized Tate parity and is additive on objects and morphisms: D(f+g)=D(f)+D(g) and D(a f)=ā^p D(f), for a∈O and ā its image in k. The proof outline records corrections and any additional obligation.

proofSteps: Expand the p-fold tensor/convolution product for a biproduct and for (f+g) in the symmetric monoidal category. The two constant words give the pure terms. Since p is prime every other word has an orbit of length p. The mixed sum of morphisms factors through an induced C_p-object; on the fixed locus it is a transfer through a perfect/flat group-ring complex, hence zero after T*. Verify this factorization on maps and its compatibility with composition, not only a direct-sum decomposition of objects. The scalar identity is the product of p copies of a; the integral Tate Hom formula reduces its action to ā^p. The factorization/coherence is a new proof target with these explicit steps, not a claim that Feng proves it.
acceptance: For p=3 check (f+g)^{⊗3}: the six mixed words form two transfers through induced objects. On a scalar a∈O the output scalar is ā³, and a=p gives zero. Perform this calculation on maps, not only objects.

nodes.title: Frobenius twists and linearization of categories
nodes.statement: For a k-linear category C define C^(p) with the same objects and Hom_C(X,Y)⊗_{k,Frob}k, composition induced by tensor product. The tautological functor Fr_C is Frobenius-semilinear and has the universal property for such functors into k-linear categories. If a specific F_p-form C₀ and scalar-extension equivalence are given, define Fr_{C₀}:C→C by fixing C₀ and applying Frobenius to scalars. A Frobenius-semilinear functor D:C→E is linearized by D∘Fr_{C₀}^{−1}. The form is data, not an automatic choice for any k-linear category.
hypotheses: Conventions C0–C4 in the reader apply, restricted to the coefficients, support and equivariance stated here.

sources.match: For a k-linear category C define C^(p) with the same objects and Hom_C(X,Y)⊗_{k,Frob}k, composition induced by tensor product. The proof outline records corrections and any additional obligation.

proofSteps: Base-change each Hom space and its bilinear composition. Prove the universal property, then use perfectness of k and the supplied form to identify the twist with C. Keep the inverse Frobenius on the source.
acceptance: In the one-object category with endomorphism algebra k, the tautological map sends a scalar to its Frobenius image after the form identification.
Over k=F₉ choose a∉F₃; precomposing D(a·id)=a³D(id) with inverse Frobenius makes the result a·id.
Changing the F_p-form changes the chosen self-equivalence data; without a form only C^(p) is canonical.

proofSteps: For inflated ordinary parity objects compare both composites with ordinary reduced CT. nodes.title: The Tate diagonal of a commutative algebra
nodes.statement: Let A be a commutative F_p-algebra with an F_p-algebra automorphism σ satisfying σ^p=1. Let A^σ be its fixed subring, Tr(a)=Σ_iσ^i(a), and Nm(a)=∏_iσ^i(a). The image Tr(A) is an ideal of A^σ. Define T^0(A)=A^σ/Tr(A), whose underlying additive group is the pinned degree-zero Tate quotient. The rule Δ_p(a)=[Nm(a)] is a unital F_p-algebra homomorphism A→T^0(A). If A is a k-algebra and σ is k-linear, Δ_p(λa)=λ^pΔ_p(a); it is Frobenius-semilinear, not generally k-linear.
hypotheses: Conventions C0–C4 in the reader apply, restricted to the coefficients, support and equivariance stated here.

sources.match: Let A be a commutative F_p-algebra with an F_p-algebra automorphism σ satisfying σ^p=1. The proof outline records corrections and any additional obligation.

proofSteps: Prove Tr(A) is additively closed and b Tr(a)=Tr(ba) for fixed b. Expand Nm(a+b); nonconstant binary words form free cyclic orbits, and each orbit sum is a transfer. Multiplicativity and the unit are direct. Match the underlying additive quotient with H0IsoNormQuotient without claiming that existing additive Tate cohomology already supplies this ring homomorphism.
acceptance: For trivial σ, Tr=0 in characteristic p and Δ_p(a)=a^p, so over F₉ it is not the identity on all scalars.
For A=B^p with cyclic factor rotation, transfer surjects onto the diagonal invariants and T^0(A)=0, including its unit as the zero ring.
For A=k[x₀,…,x_{p−1}] with cyclic permutation, Nm(x₀)=∏x_i and every mixed orbit sum in Nm(a+b) is killed; the transfer ideal is inside A^σ, not the ideal it generates in all of A.

nodes.title: Unique extension of a Tate character
nodes.statement: Let A,σ be as above, κ a perfect field of characteristic p, and A′⊂A^σ a unital subring containing Nm(A) and Tr(A). Every unital ring homomorphism χ:A′→κ vanishing on Tr(A) extends uniquely to a unital ring homomorphism χ̃:A→κ. It is given by χ̃(a)=Frob_κ^{-1}(χ(Nm(a))). This is a ring-character statement; k-linearity requires the matching chosen scalar structure.
hypotheses: Conventions C0–C4 in the reader apply, restricted to the coefficients, support and equivariance stated here.

sources.match: Let A,σ be as above, κ a perfect field of characteristic p, and A′⊂A^σ a unital subring containing Nm(A) and Tr(A). The proof outline records corrections and any additional obligation.

proofSteps: The additive-defect transfer formula and multiplicativity prove the displayed map is a ring homomorphism. For a′∈A′ use Nm(a′)=a′^p to check extension. Any other extension annihilates all transfers, so the sum of its p cyclic translates is zero. If its orbit had length p these would be distinct multiplicative characters, contradicting the existing linear-independence theorem; hence it is σ-invariant. Taking the p-th power then determines its value uniquely by perfectness.
acceptance: For trivial σ on A=k[x], A′=A and κ perfect, the formula Frob^{-1}(χ(a^p)) recovers χ(a). For a cyclic product algebra the transfer ideal contains 1, so no unital transfer-annihilating character to a nonzero field exists.

nodes.title: Frobenius twist and linearization of algebras
nodes.statement: For a commutative k-algebra A, set A^(p)=A⊗_{k,Frob}k with the tensor-product algebra structure. Its tautological map is Frobenius-semilinear and universal for such maps from A to commutative k-algebras. Given a specific F_p-form A₀ and A≅A₀⊗_{F_p}k, let Fr_{A₀} fix A₀ and send scalar λ to λ^p. Linearize a Frobenius-semilinear map f:A→B as f∘Fr_{A₀}^{−1}. Apply this to Δ_p to obtain a k-algebra map after choosing a form.

gaps.title: Uniform integral Smith theory over W(k)
gaps.detail: The existing normalized-adic supplier treats the ring of integers of a finite extension of Q_p. Prove the extension to O=W(overline(F_p)) with enhanced limits, finite-level group-ring coefficients, common constructible stratifications and uniform Tor/cohomological intervals. In particular prove the projection-formula and derived-limit comparisons for Rf!, the ambient local Rj* bound and the conservative constructible-to-ind Tate quotient comparison. Levelwise finite-Tor assertions alone do not give these conclusions. Torsion k-coefficient Smith theory and finite-dimensional pieces do not depend on this extension.

gaps.title: Étale modular Satake and parity transport
gaps.detail: Supply the equal-characteristic scheme-theoretic modular k/O branch over arbitrary separably closed F of characteristic different from p: fusion with signs, weight-functor exactness, integral dual-group reconstruction and the needed finite-Schubert/stratum geometry. Transport the JMW/LL complex-topological parity and integral Tate Hom results with their composition grading, equivariant realization, coefficient change and CT compatibility. Check the F_p-form against the geometric one. MV07 Theorem 14.1 gives a model through Z_p and scalar extension, but does not by itself document every W(k)-adic/LL compatibility. The B_dR^+ Satake roadmap is not a theorem covering this case.

gaps.title: The good-prime parity-perversity engine
gaps.detail: MR18 Corollary 1.6 uses its Theorem 1.1, an equivalence from Iwahori-constructible parity sheaves on the complex affine Grassmannian to graded exotic tilting coherent sheaves on the dual Springer resolution, with [1] corresponding to grading shift ⟨−1⟩ and E_λ to T_{−λ}. Its proof requires the modular exotic highest-weight category, Kostant–Whittaker/Soergel description and central-isogeny/product reductions. These inputs are not the characteristic-zero Springer correspondence. Establish this engine or give another proof under the same good-prime hypothesis, then the transport in G2. Do not substitute JMW16’s stronger prime bound for the promised theorem.

gaps.title: Naturality of the integral comparison on the norm image
gaps.detail: Prove the comparison F_T Psm Nm≅I_k L Psm Nm natural on all ordinary normalized integral parity maps. It suffices to prove that their Smith images have only index-zero components in the integral Tate Hom decomposition, or that every positive component is killed by coefficient reduction, with coherent choices of object identifications. Neither follows from additivity, normalization or the objectwise comparison. On the P¹ minuscule Schubert variety, a positive-index Tate morphism disproves the comparison on all Tate maps. This obligation is needed by the global Tate-cohomology consumer, not by the definition of BC.

gaps.title: A natural dual-group-equivariant comparison
gaps.detail: The CT square and character classification identify the output tilting objects, and the torus case identifies maps after torus restriction. Construct comparison components which intertwine the whole Ĥ-action and are natural in every source morphism. A sufficient route checks compatibility with each simple-root subgroup/rank-one Levi together with the torus, then uses generation of Ĥ. Faithful torus restriction only gives uniqueness of a lift, not its existence. Also check Γ-equivariance of these components for the arithmetic corollary. This is the exact gap between character equality and the natural isomorphism in Feng24 Theorem 4.20.
